newsitem.title: USA: Sovereign, First State adjust merger ratio.
newsitem.headline: Sovereign, First State adjust merger ratio.

text.p: Sovereign Bancorp Inc and First State Financial Services said on Tuesday they adjusted the exchange ratio for the planned acquisition of First State by Sovereign.

First State holders would receive the greater of $14.75 in Sovereign common stock or 1.225 Sovereign shares per First State share, they said. Previously, the exchange ratio was fixed at 1.29 shares if Sovereign's stock price were greater than $11.45.

The amendment followed the completion of Sovereign's detailed review of First State's asset quality and provided for a price adjustment in exchange for Sovereign's agreement to eliminate certain termination rights under the definitive agreement, the companies said.
They said the deal was expected to close in the first quarter 1997.
Sovereign Bancorp is the parent of Sovereign Bank and First State is the parent of First DeWitt Bank.
Under the deal, First State shareholders retained the right to terminate the agreement if the average Sovereign price fell below $8 per share.
The amendment also eliminated certain termination rights previously held by Sovereign which were specific about First States' asset quality, the companies said.
